pageCache.text:
We inspire girls to be forever curious; an enduring desire to explore, learn and grow that is the foundation for a meaningful and fulfilled life.
Learn more from our Head
When creativity meets curiosity, imagination takes flight. Paper cups become telephones, or space buggies or owls. Problems become opportunities to find new solutions, success becomes the spur to seek out the next challenge.
Our pupils love learning, our teachers love teaching, and learning too, from the girls they teach. We are never too young to start asking ‘why’ and never too old to keep on asking. Our pupils learn early on that there are some questions that simply don’t have an answer, possibly never will. It doesn’t stop them continuing to look for one!
The first thing visitors to St Christopher’s comment on is the energy; it is almost palpable, it fizzes and bubbles and frequently erupts into bursts of song or laughter, or shrieks of delight. The word bored does not exist in our language.
Not every child is an extrovert. Our assessment process is designed to allow quieter children the chance to shine, and throughout their time at St Christopher’s they are supported by our highly individualised curriculum to ensure that their contributions are heard and recognised. We value the opinions of all our pupils, not just the ones who are first with their hands up to share them.
Explore St Christopher’s
Thinking
When all the knowledge in the world can be accessed on a mobile phone, education can no longer be about filling children’s heads with facts. We teach thinking skills to enable our pupils to sift through the information overload of the age we live in; to discern, to reflect, and to apply. By this process, our pupils learn to form their own opinions and to voice them with confidence and conviction.
Thriving
As a single sex prep school, we are able to provide a safe and nurturing space for our pupils to enjoy their childhood, to take risks safely, to explore, to grow, and to change. Change is proof of growth and our graduating 11-year-olds are often quite different to the 4-year-olds they were when they joined us in Reception. This is reflected in the broad range of top senior schools they move on to.
Playing
The power of learning through play is integral to our ethos. Teamwork, compassion, how to be a good friend and a loyal ally, how to resolve disagreements respectfully are all learnt as much in the playground as they are taught in the classroom.
Creating
To create is to bring something into existence; it could be bringing a piece of music to life, rendering a piece of life in clay or on paper with paint or using words to paint another sort of picture entirely. From cupcakes to concerts, from landscapes to wordscapes, the possibilities are endless. There is a real joy in the act and pride in the finished work. Creativity is celebrated in all its forms, throughout the school.

Ethos and Aims
When you join St Christopher’s you become part of something wonderful; an exceptional community where kindness is valued, ambitions are nurtured, and endeavour is rewarded.

History of Art
Creativity in context
Art tells stories about people, places and moments in time. Through the study of History of Art, girls discover how artists have interpreted the world around them and how creative ideas continue to shape the way we see it.
As they move through Upper School, pupils explore artists, movements and techniques in greater depth, developing an understanding of the historical and cultural contexts behind the works they study. This not only enriches their own artwork but helps them make meaningful connections between the past, present and future.
History of Art encourages girls to look closely, think critically and ask thoughtful questions. Why did an artist make certain choices? How can one artwork be interpreted in different ways? Through discussion and reflection, pupils develop confidence in their own opinions while learning to appreciate the perspectives of others.
From Leonardo da Vinci to Jean-Michel Basquiat, girls encounter artists from different periods, cultures and traditions. Along the way, they discover that art is not just something to admire, but something to question, explore and enjoy.

Drama
Creating performances
Drama gives girls the opportunity to imagine, create, perform and, most importantly, have fun. Through games, storytelling, improvisation and performance, pupils build confidence, develop their creativity and learn to work closely with others.
Girls enjoy drama lessons from Reception, and from Year 4 they are taught by a specialist drama teacher. Alongside developing performance skills, they learn to collaborate, communicate clearly and support one another as part of an ensemble. Whether speaking to a small group or performing to a full audience, girls are encouraged to take pride in their contribution and grow in confidence.
Performance is an important part of drama at St Christopher’s. Every year group takes part in an annual production, ranging from Shakespeare and musical theatre to original performances created by the girls themselves. These productions are carefully designed to ensure that every child has the opportunity to participate, develop their skills and enjoy the experience of performing.
At St Christopher’s, drama is about more than being on stage. It helps girls find their voice, express their ideas and discover the confidence to try something new.

Music
Making music together
Music is a joyful part of life at St Christopher’s, and every girl is encouraged to participate, perform and develop a lifelong love of music.
Through classroom lessons, choirs, ensembles and performances, girls explore singing, rhythm, instrumental playing, composition and listening. They learn how to perform with confidence, work as part of an ensemble and express themselves creatively through music.
We are a singing school and celebrate the happiness, confidence and sense of community that singing together brings. Every class enjoys weekly singing lessons and choir rehearsals, and every girl belongs to one of our choirs: Little Voices, Middle School Choir or Upper School Choir.
Music making extends far beyond the classroom. Girls can take part in a range of ensembles, including Chamber Choir, Orchestra, String Groups, Wind Band and Guitar Group, giving them regular opportunities to rehearse and perform together.
For those wishing to develop their skills further, we offer individual instrumental and singing lessons with a team of experienced professional musicians. Lessons are available in a wide range of instruments, including piano, violin, cello, guitar, flute, clarinet, saxophone and voice, and pupils have the opportunity to take ABRSM examinations throughout the year.
Whether performing in an assembly, school production, concert or informal recital, every girl is encouraged to share her music with confidence and pride.

Science
Questioning and investigating
Science begins with curiosity. Why do things float? How do plants grow? Could there be life beyond Earth? At St Christopher’s, girls are encouraged to ask big questions, investigate possible answers and develop the confidence to think like scientists.
As part of our STEAM programme, science is woven throughout school life. Girls learn that the most exciting discoveries often happen when different subjects come together, whether that is combining science with technology, engineering, art or maths. Through investigation, experimentation and problem-solving, they learn to think critically, test ideas and embrace mistakes as an essential part of learning.
We believe every child should see science as something they can engage with, enjoy and succeed in. From exploring environmental issues to investigating how things work, girls develop the knowledge and skills needed to understand an ever-changing world. Along the way, they learn that science is not simply about finding answers, but about asking thoughtful questions too.
Learning extends far beyond the classroom. Our parent community regularly shares its expertise, while visiting STEAM ambassadors, hands-on workshops and trips to places such as the Science Museum help bring learning to life. These experiences broaden horizons, spark new interests and show girls the many different ways science can be part of their future.
Pupils were consulted and worked alongside our architect on creating the school site masterplan whilst learning about sustainable building development. You can watch the film here.

Learning Enrichment
Supporting every learner
Learning Enrichment is woven into everyday school life and classroom learning at St Christopher’s.
Our Learning Enrichment team works closely with teachers to identify and support pupils whenever additional challenge or support may be beneficial. Because every child learns differently, support is flexible and responsive, helping each girl to develop confidence, make progress and achieve her full potential.
This support may take a variety of forms, including adapted resources, targeted interventions, small-group teaching, reading support, revision and booster sessions, or opportunities for further challenge and extension. Where appropriate, some pupils may also benefit from more personalised one-to-one support with a member of the Learning Enrichment team.
By working in partnership with pupils, teachers and families, we ensure that every girl receives the encouragement and support she needs to thrive both academically and personally.

Clubs
Fun and learning are not confined to the school day
Each term we offer over 50 morning, daytime and after-school clubs. We encourage our pupils to try new activities and to further explore their passions. Clubs are led by internal staff and highly qualified visiting staff.
There is something for everyone, from sports clubs to language learning, from running to ukulele, from storytelling to architecture, from puppet making to puzzles, from stop motion animation to singing while digitally doodling.

Art
Creativity in action
Art at St Christopher’s is a space to explore, experiment and create. Girls are encouraged to take risks, express themselves and enjoy the creative process, developing confidence in their own ideas rather than striving for perfection.
Creativity is woven throughout school life, and girls work with a wide range of materials and techniques, including drawing, painting, clay, textiles, photography, collage and digital media. As they develop their skills, they learn to observe closely, think creatively and take pride in producing work that is uniquely their own.
We enrich classroom learning through participation in local and national projects and competitions, including the Hampstead Art Fair, the National Gallery’s Take One Picture, the Royal Academy’s Young Artists’ Summer Show and collaborative projects with institutions such as the Wallace Collection and Tate.
Our London location provides endless inspiration, and girls regularly visit museums and galleries to experience art first-hand. At the end of each year, families are invited to celebrate the girls’ achievements at Around St Christopher’s an exhibition that showcases the creativity, imagination and progress of every pupil.

Digital Technology
Coding and creating
Technology is changing the world at an extraordinary pace. The question is not whether our girls will use technology, but how they will use it. Will they simply consume it, or will they help shape what comes next?
At St Christopher’s, digital technology is about curiosity, creativity and problem-solving. Girls learn to use technology thoughtfully and responsibly, developing the confidence to navigate an increasingly digital world. Alongside practical skills, they learn to make informed decisions, understand their online responsibilities and appreciate the impact technology can have on school, work and everyday life.
We want our pupils to see technology as a tool for exploration and innovation. Whether researching a new idea, collaborating with classmates or presenting their learning in imaginative ways, girls discover how digital skills can support learning across the curriculum and beyond.
Most importantly, we encourage girls to become creators, not just consumers, of technology. Programming begins in Year 1 with Bee Bots and develops through Scratch and Logo before progressing to programming VEX robots in Year 6. Along the way, pupils create films, design 3D models using CAD software, build collaboratively in Minecraft, produce stop-motion animations and develop eye-catching posters and presentations.
Through these experiences, girls learn to think critically, solve problems creatively and approach new technologies with confidence and curiosity. We believe these are the skills that will help them thrive, whatever the future may bring.

English
We teach English to learn about ourselves and others. From Reception to Year 6, English is about nurturing a love of language and stories. It enables communication, helping girls make sense of the world.
Stories have the power to spark imagination, build empathy and open new ways of thinking. Through reading, writing, speaking and listening, our girls discover different perspectives, develop their own voice and learn to express themselves with confidence and creativity.
Our English curriculum is rich, ambitious and designed to inspire a lifelong love of language. From the first stages of phonics and early reading to thoughtful literary analysis and sophisticated creative writing, girls are encouraged to explore, question and communicate with growing independence. We continually reflect on and refine our teaching, ensuring that learning remains engaging, relevant and responsive to the needs of each year group.
English sits at the heart of school life because it underpins every area of learning. When girls can articulate their ideas clearly, they are empowered to think more deeply, ask more searching questions and make meaningful connections across subjects. Whether crafting a compelling story, presenting an argument or discussing a challenging text, they develop the confidence to share their thinking with others.
Above all, we want every girl to leave St Christopher’s as a curious and enthusiastic reader. Books transport us to different worlds, introduce us to memorable characters and inspire us to see life in new ways. The joy of reading is one of the greatest gifts we can give our pupils, and one that we hope will stay with them long after they leave us.

Geography
The world around us
What is a biome? Why do people move from one place to another? How does weather differ from climate? And how can we help shape a better future?
Geography begins with questions. At St Christopher’s, girls are encouraged to explore the world with curiosity and compassion, developing an understanding of both the physical processes that shape our planet and the people who live on it. From their local surroundings to distant continents, they learn to see the connections between places, environments and communities.
Through enquiry, investigation and discussion, pupils develop the skills to think critically about the world around them. They analyse maps, interpret data, explore different viewpoints and draw on a wide range of sources, from books and fieldwork to digital technologies and expert insight. As their understanding grows, so too does their awareness of the challenges and opportunities facing our planet.
We hope geography inspires girls to look beyond their own experiences and develop a truly global perspective. By exploring issues such as migration, sustainability, climate and human impact, pupils begin to understand how individual actions can contribute to positive change. The change-makers and innovators of the future start by asking thoughtful questions today.
Geography is at its most fascinating when experienced first-hand. Whether investigating weather patterns around the school, mapping the local area or braving the elements while orienteering on Hampstead Heath, girls learn through practical exploration and discovery. These real-world experiences bring learning to life and help nurture a lifelong curiosity about the world and our place within it.

History
The past is with us in the present
History is full of fascinating questions. If history is written by the victors, what happened to those on the losing side? What stories might they have told? At St Christopher’s, girls are encouraged to think beyond the facts, question assumptions and explore the many voices that have shaped our world.
Through the study of history, pupils develop a deeper understanding of people, places and events across time. As they move through the school, they travel chronologically through the history of Britain, building a coherent picture of the past while developing the knowledge and skills needed for future study. Along the way, they broaden their horizons through the study of other cultures and civilisations, from Ancient Egypt to the Kingdom of Benin.
Curiosity sits at the centre of our approach. Girls learn to scrutinise sources, weigh evidence and consider different perspectives. They are encouraged to think critically, debate thoughtfully and ask searching questions, developing the judgement and confidence to form their own conclusions.
History comes alive through hands-on experiences and cross-curricular learning. On any given day, girls might be building Ancient Egyptian pyramids from Lego, baking cakes inspired by the Great Fire of London or crafting persuasive arguments about the Glorious Revolution. By combining history with philosophy, drama, outdoor learning and creative projects, we help pupils see that the past is not something distant and fixed, but something rich, complex and endlessly fascinating.

Languages
Many voices, one community
Bulgarian, Chinese, English, French, German, Greek, Hebrew, Italian, Japanese, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Swahili and Swedish are all spoken within our community. For many of our pupils and staff, speaking more than one language is part of everyday life, creating a rich environment where different cultures, perspectives and experiences are celebrated.
Learning a language opens doors. It encourages curiosity about the world, builds confidence in communication and helps girls see things from a different perspective. From Reception to Year 6, all pupils learn Spanish with a specialist teacher, developing their speaking, listening, reading and writing skills through engaging and interactive lessons.
Our approach is practical, creative and full of opportunities to use language with confidence. Through songs, games, role play and performances, girls discover that languages are not simply something to study but a way to connect with people and cultures around the world. Along the way, they develop the critical thinking skills that support learning across the curriculum.
In Years 5 and 6, pupils also learn Latin, giving them valuable insight into the roots of many modern languages. French is a popular club from Reception onwards, providing even more opportunity for girls to explore the joy of languages.
Our pupils leave St Christopher’s with the confidence to communicate, an appreciation of different cultures and a lifelong curiosity about the wider world.

Mathematics
For every problem there is a solution waiting to be found.
Mathematics is about far more than numbers. It is about spotting patterns, thinking creatively and finding solutions to problems. Some problems are fiendishly tricky, others delight in their simplicity, but all encourage girls to question, explore and think in new ways.
From Reception to Year 6, girls develop a secure understanding of mathematical concepts while building the confidence to tackle increasingly complex challenges. Learning is carefully structured, but curiosity is always encouraged. Through investigation, collaboration and independent thinking, girls learn that there is often more than one route to a solution and that mistakes are an important part of the journey.
We want our pupils to see mathematics everywhere. Whether measuring ingredients for cupcakes, exploring patterns in nature or solving a puzzle with friends, girls are encouraged to make connections between classroom learning and the world around them. Our much-loved Maths Monkey regularly joins girls at home, inspiring families to discover the everyday maths hidden in baking, shopping, travelling and play.
Creativity plays an important role in our approach. Recent projects have included Maths through Stories, where girls created their own mathematical picture books, Gnome Homes, which combined numerical thinking with 2D and 3D design, and Beyond Sudoku, an exploration of Japanese puzzles and logical reasoning. These experiences bring mathematics to life, showing girls that the subject is rich, imaginative and full of possibilities.
We want every girl to leave St Christopher’s as a confident problem-solver: someone who approaches challenges with resilience, thinks critically and remains endlessly curious about how things work.

Inspection reports
Inspection Reports
As a member school of the Girls’ Schools’ Association (GSA) and the Independent Association of Preparatory Schools (IAPS), St Christopher’s School is inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI). ISI is the organisation appointed by the Department for Education to inspect association independent schools in England. Their inspection reports inform the Department for Education on the extent to which the statutory Independent School Standards are met. Additionally, the inspection reports on the school’s accessibility plan under Schedule 10 of the Equality Act 2010 and the ban on corporal punishment under section 548 of the Education Act 1996.

Sport
Active, confident, involved
Sport is an important part of life at St Christopher’s. Whether girls are learning a new skill, representing the school in competition or simply enjoying being active with friends, sport helps them build confidence, resilience, teamwork and a lifelong enjoyment of physical activity.
From the excitement of energetic games such as Hero Chicken in the Lower School to competitive fixtures in the Upper School, girls are encouraged to challenge themselves, support one another and celebrate both individual and team achievements.
PE lessons develop core skills including fitness, balance, coordination and agility. In games lessons, younger girls focus on fundamental movement skills, while older pupils build their understanding of team sports and prepare for fixtures and tournaments. Across the year, girls enjoy a wide range of activities including netball, football, hockey, gymnastics, cross-country, cricket and athletics. Swimming forms part of the curriculum in Year 3, and by Year 4 every girl represents the school as part of a team.
All sport is taught by specialist teachers who are passionate about making physical activity enjoyable, accessible and rewarding for every child. For girls who would like even more opportunities to be active, a wide range of clubs is available, including judo, dance, basketball and table tennis, alongside squad training sessions and additional coaching throughout the year.
At St Christopher’s, sport is about far more than winning. It is about developing healthy habits, discovering new strengths, building friendships and having fun.

Trips
Learning through experience
Some of the most memorable learning happens beyond the classroom. Trips and visits give girls the opportunity to explore new places, bring their learning to life and spend time together in different settings.
Throughout the year, pupils visit museums, galleries, historic sites, farms and places of natural interest to support their learning across the curriculum. Some visits help girls deepen their understanding of a particular topic, while others encourage teamwork, independence, creativity or social awareness. Whatever the destination, each experience helps broaden their horizons and build lasting memories.
We make the most of everything London has to offer, with visits to landmarks such as St Paul’s Cathedral, Shakespeare’s Globe, the National Gallery and Tate Modern, alongside many lesser-known places that spark curiosity and inspire learning. Regular theatre trips also give girls the chance to experience performances and storytelling beyond the school gates.
From Year 4 onwards, all pupils enjoy an annual residential trip. These experiences give girls the opportunity to develop confidence, resilience and independence while strengthening friendships. Beginning with a three-day activity trip in Year 4, residential visits become longer as the girls move through the school. Recent destinations have included Wales, Cornwall and Devon, where pupils have enjoyed outdoor adventures, team challenges and shared experiences they’ll remember for years to come.
